chunks: It is God who sends the winds that raise the clouds. Then We drive the clouds towards the land that was dead, and restore the earth to life after it had died. So will be the Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran use the revival of dead land as a metaphor for resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Fatir is often cited to demonstrate the logical necessity of resurrection (Nushur) through the observable miracle of agricultural revival. The imagery of 'dead land' being brought to life by wind-carried rain serves as a tangible proof (Burhan) for the unseen reality of the soul's return, reinforcing the concept of God as the Originator (Al-Fattar) who initiates creation from nothingness. This analogy underscores that just as physical matter responds to divine command, so too will the human body and spirit be reconstituted for accountability.
